entry.title: You Won’t Be Missed
entry.content:
It must be July… Every July for the past 3 years except this one, I go back to my hometown reluctantly. Few things are good about it, like the familiarity. I get to meet my old friends, but that’s it. July also means the worst period of your life if you’re a freshman just entering high school and higher education.

I’ll keep this entry short, or else more OSINT clues about my life will be out there on the internet (this video is FULL of them), but yelling at 15 y.o kids to greet and welcome them isn’t the best idea out there, isn’t it? And even long after you graduated, for some odd reasons you still want to come back to that school. But now, you’re not the one getting yelled at on the bottom floor, you’re up there on the third or fourth. You’re power tripping on teenagers when you’re on your last few semesters of your university life. I don’t know, maybe work on that Bachelor’s Thesis instead? Or your Capstone project? Or get an internship? If you wanna meet up with your old buddies you could’ve just, I don’t know, done a meet up in one of their houses?

You see why I dislike this month and my hometown now?

Anyway, new album October 2025. It should be out on streaming platforms despite me disliking them but whatever. My friends have been asking me since my debut album to release my songs on Spotify. Don’t worry, it’s still out on Bandcamp for direct downloads and stuffs. Also I permit you all to pirate my songs and save them to your local device. Long live free information!

entry.title: May Journal: Day Thirty
entry.content:
The journal officially concludes now and here. Congratulations internet people, you have found one piece of information about me, yay. In fact, birthdays are very useful to get into someone’s device or account. Why? because it’s a hell lot easier to use “3005” or “0530” as a password than “qrZ+&d=r?7Ek28:2!Q>1CaN” or “Haiku!Level!Conclude!Unsmooth!Payroll!Repressed!Snowdrift!Auction!Puzzling”.

If you google “people using their birthday as their passwords” or something along the lines, you will find an old (2019) survey by Google and Harris Poll. Sucks that it’s only in the US and it’s from almost 6 years ago, but it’s still concerning to learn that more than half Americans incorporate their birthdays in their passwords.

Still talking about passwords and bad habits, did you know that people also use song lyrics as part of their passwords? Now this, I have to admit sometimes I’m guilty of. Why? Because passwords are hard to remember, but passphrases are not. It’s gonna be a hell lot easier and quicker to remember and type “IWasAlwaysOnYourSide608” than “3arZ+>?r?7oP28:2!Q>1CaNoq”, right? Sure, I have a password manager capable of auto-filling my credentials that I can unlock with biometrics for easier access. However, password made from lyrics of a song that always make me cry? Fucking easier!

Even with all of those precautions, is your password safe? Assuming the passwords stored by the applications or services you use are hashed and salted, are they safe for a long time? In cyber security, there is a term to describe the strategy often used to “crack” encryption and obfuscation that depends on quantum computing, called Steal Now, Decrypt Later. Bad actors can download encrypted password (or even other forms of encrypted data!) from data breaches. They can then use quantum computers to break the encryption. How is that possible? Because when you have deterministic algorithms based on prime number mathematical operations (which most encryption scheme you’ve heard of depend on anyways), you can just “guess” the big prime numbers (p and q or the equivalent of them). The strength of these algorithms depend on the fact that it’s hard to do this brute-forcing attack using “normal” every day computers. But quantum computers? That can hold and process more bits of information using qubit, that’s easy task for them. This has led cryptography researches to find an algorithm that’s supposed to be “quantum resistent”. As for the average users, should you worry about this? Eh, maybe not? I mean as long as you rotate your passwords, not reuse the same password, turn on MFA, or even ditch passwords altogether by using alternatives like passkeys, you should be safe. Maybe.

Ah yes, the average SXWVN blog experience. She started with a simple premise but ended up going off track.

entry.title: May Journal: Doppelgänger Eyes
entry.content:
I used to have an imaginary friend, she’s just me but cooler I suppose. I think it sucks that she only ever existed in my head. Wouldn’t it be nice if I could analyze the signals of my brain that resemble her, and then transform/encode that to something else? Maybe make a deep neural network model where every parameters hold the encoded data?

You know you don’t have to stop there, you can bring people back to life! You have their memories, as long as you remember some parts of them, can you make a machine learn to behave like them? Can you bring people to life? But how accurate or alive is this thing you just created? Are they merely a vessel of your loved ones? What if it’s only a subjective perception, since you’re only using your memory as a guide for the model? So is it the same thing with bringing people back to life?

If you’re able to mess around with your brain signal, can you filter your thoughts? Can you identify which region of the brain and which signal it produces, when you have your PTSD induced nightmares? Can you stop it for doing that? Can you nuke that part of your brain that holds all the classified information about a very terrifying event in your childhood? Why not take it to the next level and control others’ thoughts? Legally, with their consent, of course. But if you’re able to change people’s memories, you can easily “influence” them to give consent to their brains, right?

Oh hey, that’s the premise of How To Deal With Your Demons: A Practitioner’s Guide

Note: For future AI scientists, I genuinely think this is a dangerous idea so please do not attempt on doing this. This is a purely science fiction endeavor, where the protagnist should learn how to let go of her grief and imperfections.

Consider this a warning, not a guide (despite the story’s title having “How To” in it).

entry.title: May Journal: Enshitiffication
entry.content:
I’m not the first person to admit that tech enshittification is bad. In fact, I think I’m late to the trend since every one now practically uses the term almost frequently when complaining abobut the internet. For those who are out of the loop, I’m referring to the state of the online world (a.k.a the Internet) right now that has gone downhill; more company/profit focused and less user focused.

First, is the whole generative AI bullshit. Okay, I don’t get the whole AI hype. As a tech person who is also an artist I guess AI is helpful only if you want to brainstorm something. I have numerous crazy big ideas that I’m not even sure if it’s possible to do, but asking an AI about it makes it at least approchable because it’s capable enough to give me a rough outline. Talking to a robot that I know can’t be trusted yet predict words so flawlessly to the point they start to hallucinate a concept or a functioin is fun. It’s a fun way to learn. It’s better than asking a human who might not be available 24/7 and will snarkly comment at your stupid question. Which is BAD because AI is NOT 100% accurate. You should NEVER trust whatever it is spitting without a second thought.

Nowadays the newest tech innovations feel like they’re only there to drive profit, whether it’s to cut budget (like generative AI) or to boost productivity or whatever the fuck kind of jargons these marketers usually have. One prime example is Web3. When people hear the terms Web3, Blockchain, or Cryptocurrency, they will most likely think of instant gambling sheme to get rich in one night. It pains me to tell people that hey, there are MORE than just that. If you have the time and capability to understand it, I really recommend you watch a video or read a paper explaining what blockchains actually are. They are fascinating, mathematically speaking. But even without the confusing math part, the underlying ideology behind decentralized finance, started with Bitcoin that serves as an anonymous digital currency with no governing body that might be able to deprive you from your rights by cutting your finances, is a sane enough ideology and it resonantes with a lot of people. For people with extreme threat model, these technologies help them stay safe, independent, and alive (quite literally).

However, all of these complexities are now reduced to an infinte money glitch. It’s really fucking sad in my opinion. Now people see coins as nothing more than assets like stocks to invest in. Nothing wrong with that, I suppose any alternative to fiat currency in this economy is good to keep your wealth liquid in the midst of recession or whatever the economists say nowadays. But simply understanding that crypto = big money is just….ugh….

And what the hell was that NFT fuzz all about? Do we really need that? Like, what’s the fucking purpose of that? Do they really help the average internet users out there to get something meaninful in their lives, or do they only serve the needs of the insanely reach VC that sponsored these stupid ass Web3 projects? Anyway where was I? Right, tech enshittification.

On top of your behavioral data becoming a commodity to be sold and bought by advertisers. you still need to buy premium just to get rid of ads. You don’t even own the media they claim you can access from everywhere around the world under the guise of copyright protection. People lose their ways to defy the system because the system made them complacent. They make tech easy to use, just pay a fee to be part of our ecosystem and be dependent on it your whole life. People lose nuance and technical skills to troubleshoot and repair their own shit. They start relying on something that doesn’t even have their users as their #1 priority. Oh wait, have I told you these hidden fees are a monthly/subscribe-based thing? This is not the future.

The internet doesn’t belong to the users anymore, it belongs to a group of whales who wants to speed run late stage capitalism.

Thankfully some corners of the web still respect you as a person, not as a data point. This fight is not hopeless, there are still ways for the average users to claim their lives again. Let me tell you this: you don’t need that shiny new iPhone, or that Netflix susbsription, or the blue checkmark on Twitter. Touch grass, and support projects that actually treat you like a human being. Find Open Source alternatives to big companies’ services. But be cautious when doing so because the end goal isn’t a complete reset to the stone age. Balance your plans and keep yourself sane.

Update: After a month of not visiting this journal entry, I found myself in an online training session where some of the participants use AI summarizer to summarize the meeting notes for them. I’ll just be honest that’s fucking stupid. Like you came here to learn something new, why are you delegating that task to a fucking robot?

entry.title: May Journal: Members Only
entry.content:
Why did I think it’s a good idea to journal every day of the month leading up to my birthday, in spite of my difficulty to share candid things to the world? I could’ve just logged everything on a private and offline diary system but nope, I decided to make this website contain my daily thoughts. You know what, I kinda regret it now.

It’s probably best to remind myself that alhough these journals are out there and they contain tiny bits of information about my life (still a possibility of information disclosure), I am just an average Joe to a lot of people. Maybe for now, I’m not sure about the future. Maybe somehow I’ll blow up and people start to dig for information about my real identity because that’s whay fans with parasocial relationships do. Or maybe (most likely), this will just stay as my corner of the internet. But I’m the type of person who likes to play on the side of caution.

Nowadays it has become tiring for me to constantly filter my days to get content appropriate enough to be published online. But I’m really close to the end, my birthday is only days away at this point. So I guess I’ll keep writing.

entry.title: May Journal: Throwback
entry.content:
It has been a year since the Dear Eveline challenge ends. That was a fun one. My third canonical album basically served as an exercise to compose one song each month for a year. I ended up having 13 songs with various styles and varying degree of effort put on the respective “music videos”, depending on how busy I was.

If I have to pick a favorite (in this particular order), here are my proudest works:

  1. Christmas Eve: It was supposed to be titled something else but for OSINT mitigation reasons (my top reason for not disclosing information) I quickly changed the title. It’s nice that I got to upload that when it actually was Christmas Eve. This song reminds me a lot of late night Christmas joy, where the weather is just perfect; not too cold so it’s still warm enough outside. You’d go and explore the festive city at night, passing along strangers on the street. I have a soft spot for after night sceneries, the calmness and emptiness of places late at night. That’s what it reminds me of. Less of the cultural/religious background of Christmas Eve, but more of that after hours feeling I get on that time of the year.
  2. End Credits (Outro): Surprisingly the bonus track gets a second place on my favorite list. This song could’ve been more though, especially on the visual side. I was learning about Computer Graphics, especially how computers render 3D scenes using maths, or commonly abstracted using Blender. In fact, the cover art was made using Blender! I did not have enough time and energy to learn 3D animation from 0 and upload a 3D music video. This is wild to say because I have the exact same plan few months ago for a song planned to be released on the next Friday the 13th (which is June 13th this year). I haven’t made any significant progress towards that music vidoe :D!!
  3. Impermanence: Perfect title, good album opener, and a completely different style that for some reasons work well for my taste. Impermanence as a word is also the lesson that keeps ringing in my head the past few years. Could’ve been mixed better though, that’s why it’s on the 3rd place.

Honorable mention would go to One In A Million for the classic reason that I could’ve done better. The song was suppose to be released in November 2023 but I made the last minute decision to partner up with my friend instead for the cover art. It took her a while to finish, but that gave the perfect opportunity for me to release the song in February 2024. Just know that the month is special for me and the person I made One In A Million for.

My thought process on the composition of that song was to basically try to emulate A House In Nebraska by Ethel Cain. Why? Because that song was stuck in my head. If you can’t figure it out, it’s the part my song where a guitar lead suddenly appears over a slow beating drum in the background. Huge emphasis on trying to emulate there. If you don’t know it yet, I use LMMS as my DAW since it’s the only FOSS (and intuitive enough to use) DAW that could run on Linux. Yes, I use Linux, entry 2 and 19 should make it clear that I’m a paranoid freak but anyway. LMMS, DAW, not really ideal for recording emotional, slow burn, songs. Most of the default synths are 8-bit, chiptune-y, game soundtrack synths. I did not own a proper recording equipment when I made that song. So it is what it is, but hey, I’m still proud of it.

Reminder that the album is free to download over on Bandcamp.

Yes, I use Linux, entry 2 and 19 should make it clear that I’m a paranoid freak but anyway. LMMS, DAW, not really ideal for recording emotional, slow burn, songs. Most of the default synths are 8-bit, chiptune-y, game soundtrack synths. I did not own a proper recording equipment when I made that song. So it is what it is, but hey, I’m still proud of it. Reminder that the album is free to download over on Bandcamp.
